declaration: Nigeria is built by ordinary people who keep showing up.
Persistence, trust and faithful work turn a country's hopes into real things.
Watch each trailer, then ask what you can build where you stand.
teaser: Building the Nigeria God Intends is a 30-day series on ordinary Nigerians who built with persistence, trust and showing up, starting after these trailers.

days.takeaway: The series begins with a simple claim: the Nigeria God intends is built by ordinary people who keep at it.
days.reflect: What does a Nigeria God intends look like in your street, school or church?
days.doToday: Tell one family member what you would most like to see built in Nigeria in your lifetime.

days.takeaway: The series title is a promise to watch closely. What is built is shaped by the choices of people who are willing to start.
days.reflect: What is one thing you are willing to start, even if it is small?
days.doToday: Write down one small thing you can start this week to help build your community.

days.takeaway: Some of the people who built did so by showing up again and again, even when no one was watching or cheering.
days.reflect: Where in your life do you show up faithfully, and who notices?
days.doToday: Show up for one commitment today that no one will praise you for.

days.takeaway: Trust alone is not enough. Trust must be matched by steady action and wise, faithful work.
days.reflect: Where have you trusted God in words but not yet in action?
days.doToday: Take one practical step that matches a trust you have been talking about.

days.takeaway: This trailer looks at Dangote's refinery and the difference between persistence and the myth of the self-made success.
days.reflect: Who helped you get where you are, and how do you honour them?
days.doToday: Thank one person who helped you build something, and tell them specifically what they gave you.

days.takeaway: Chioma Ajunwa's story is about a comeback. Getting back up after a setback is part of building.
days.reflect: What setback have you been trying to recover from, and what would a comeback look like?
days.doToday: Write one honest sentence about a setback and one step you can take to get back up.

days.takeaway: Innoson's story moves from spare parts to a vehicle factory. Big things often begin with small pieces that are carefully put together.
days.reflect: What small piece are you holding right now that could become part of something larger?
days.doToday: Take one small piece of a project you care about and finish it today.

days.takeaway: The vaccinators who kept returning show what faithful service looks like. Coming back again, day after day, is a form of love.
days.reflect: Who are the people in your community who keep coming back to serve, and how could you encourage them?
days.doToday: Encourage one person who serves quietly and faithfully in your community.

days.takeaway: Ajaokuta is a story of a giant steel plant and the missing links behind it. A nation is built when every link is connected.
days.reflect: What missing link in your own life or community could be connected with a little more care?
days.doToday: Identify one missing link in a project you are part of, and reach out to fill it.
